sqlQuery.name: Coords
sqlQuery.sql: WITH ids AS ( SELECT t.source_id , t.project_id , split_part(t.source_id, ':', 1) AS strain , split_part(t.source_id, ':', 2) AS ref_seq , split_part(split_part(t.source_id, ':', 3), '-', 1)::integer AS ref_start , split_part(split_part(t.source_id, ':', 3), '-', 2)::integer AS ref_end FROM (##WDK_ID_SQL##) t ) SELECT ids.source_id , ids.project_id , ids.strain , ids.ref_seq , ids.ref_start , ids.ref_end -- unambiguous only because strain names contain no underscore while -- reference sequence IDs do (e.g. Pf3D7_01_v3), so the first '_' always -- ends the strain name. , ids.strain || '_' || ids.ref_seq AS strain_seq_id , ids.ref_start + COALESCE(off.offset_start, 0) AS strain_start , ids.ref_end + COALESCE(off.offset_end, 0) AS strain_end -- Clamped at zero: a segment lying inside a deletion legitimately -- inverts (the reference bases do not exist in this strain), which -- would otherwise yield a negative length. strain_start/strain_end -- above are deliberately NOT clamped -- the inversion -- (strain_end < strain_start) is the signal the BED feature provider -- checks for and rejects loudly. , GREATEST( (ids.ref_end + COALESCE(off.offset_end, 0)) - (ids.ref_start + COALESCE(off.offset_start, 0)) + 1 , 0 ) AS strain_length , tn.name AS organism FROM ids JOIN dots.ExternalNaSequence ens ON ens.source_id = ids.ref_seq JOIN sres.TaxonName tn ON tn.taxon_id = ens.taxon_id AND tn.name_class = 'scientific name' LEFT JOIN ( SELECT seg.source_id -- Boundary asymmetry is deliberate: '<' for the start offset, '<=' for -- the end. An indel exactly at ref_start lies INSIDE the segment, so it -- shifts the end but not the start. An off-by-one here is silent -- the -- coordinates just come out wrong, with no error anywhere. , SUM(CASE WHEN i.location < seg.ref_start THEN i.shift ELSE 0 END) AS offset_start , SUM(CASE WHEN i.location <= seg.ref_end THEN i.shift ELSE 0 END) AS offset_end FROM ids seg , dots.ExternalNaSequence ens2 , study.protocolappnode pan , apidb.indel i WHERE ens2.source_id = seg.ref_seq AND pan.name = CONCAT(seg.strain, '_Indel') AND i.protocol_app_node_id = pan.protocol_app_node_id AND i.na_sequence_id = ens2.na_sequence_id AND i.location <= seg.ref_end -- Grouping on seg.source_id (the whole PK) makes one-row-per-PK true by -- construction; one protocol_app_node_id spans EVERY sequence of a strain, so -- grouping on coordinate fields alone conflated segments on different -- sequences and summed a foreign chromosome's shifts into both. GROUP BY seg.source_id -- NOT redundant, and not to be "cleaned up": it is here so that a strain -- name resolving to two protocol app nodes on one sequence yields -- DUPLICATE rows per PK and a loud WDK error, rather than silently -- summing two strains' shifts. 126 strain names map to more than one -- organism, so this is reachable by a data change alone. , i.protocol_app_node_id ) off ON off.source_id = ids.source_id
